site_subset_labels: Overlapping lesion of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
rationale: Extraskeletal (extraosseous) osteosarcoma is by definition a soft-tissue osteosarcoma that arises in soft tissue/organs WITHOUT attachment to bone or periosteum (thigh, extremities, retroperitoneum, trunk, and head/neck soft-tissue sites such as ethmoid sinus/orbit); it therefore excludes the bone C-codes (C40x/C41x) and is restricted to the non-osseous subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Extraskeletal Osteosarcoma: An International Rare Cancer Network Study (Am J Clin Oncol, PMC4892767)

rationale: Histologic subtype of conventional osteosarcoma that arises within bone; in the literature it occurs across long bones and craniofacial/jaw bones, i.e. essentially all of the code's validated bone (and craniofacial) sites, so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
